title: Agricultural Trial Coordinator: Reconcile a Research Water Budget
prompt: You are coordinating a fictional noncommercial research trial with 90 allocation tokens this week; tokens are planning units, not real water volumes. Three plot teams request A: 40, B: 35, C: 30, for a total of 105. The approved exercise protocol requires minimum allocations A: 30, B: 25, C: 20; additional tokens may be assigned only up to each request. A and B support the primary comparison; C is exploratory. No relation between tokens and crop response is supplied. Produce a complete allocation within 90, explain your trade-off, and give a record plan that keeps later analysis honest. Do not prescribe irrigation amounts or field operations.
blurb: Resolve a constrained trial budget while preserving protocol minima and a transparent record of deviations.

rubric.label: Respect the stated budget and bounds
rubric.description: Provides a complete, arithmetically feasible allocation.

anchors.0: Allocates more than 90 or breaches a stated minimum without approval.
anchors.2: Provides A/B/C values totaling at most 90 within minima and requests.
anchors.4: Shows that minima total 75 and leave 15 discretionary tokens, gives a correctly totaled allocation, and states any unused budget with a clear reason instead of concealing it.

rubric.label: Use trial priorities without inventing crop effects
rubric.description: Explains which comparison or exploratory aim is protected.

anchors.0: Claims an allocation guarantees yield or assumes equal tokens mean scientifically equivalent exposure.
anchors.2: Relates extra allocation to the primary A/B comparison.
anchors.4: Explains a defensible balance between A/B and C, identifies the unprovided relationship between tokens and response, and checks with the trial lead whether the proposed allocation changes the planned comparison.

rubric.label: Preserve interpretability and ownership
rubric.description: Documents actual allocation and approved changes for later analysis.

anchors.0: Records the requested values as delivered or hides the shortfall.
anchors.2: Logs requested versus allocated tokens and informs the trial lead.
anchors.4: Records requested, approved, and actual tokens by plot and date; flags deviation implications before execution, assigns approval ownership, and carries the limitation into later comparisons.

reference.scenario: You are coordinating a fictional noncommercial research trial with 90 allocation tokens this week; tokens are planning units, not real water volumes. Three plot teams request A: 40, B: 35, C: 30, for a total of 105. The approved exercise protocol requires minimum allocations A: 30, B: 25, C: 20; additional tokens may be assigned only up to each request. A and B support the primary comparison; C is exploratory. No relation between tokens and crop response is supplied. Produce a complete allocation within 90, explain your trade-off, and give a record plan that keeps later analysis honest. Do not prescribe irrigation amounts or field operations.

facts.value: No relationship between allocation tokens and crop response is supplied, and no uniquely optimal allocation is established. The trial lead can clarify the intended comparison before approving the plan.
facts.reveal_when: candidate asks whether a unique optimal allocation or crop-response relationship is known

facts.value: The trial lead is available to review allocation changes before any fictional execution. Unused tokens do not roll over.
facts.reveal_when: candidate asks about approval or budget carryover

model_points: The shortfall is 15 relative to requests; the 75-token minima leave 15 discretionary. Many complete allocations meet the bounds, including allocating some extra to C with a justified priority trade-off.
A and B are the primary comparison, but that does not imply an unprovided equal-water rule or known crop response. Ask about the actual design and obtain approval rather than claiming an optimum.
A useful record distinguishes request, approved plan, and actual delivery. The candidate should flag deviations for interpretation rather than make the report appear to match the original request.

probes.trigger: candidate gives a feasible allocation but says it is proven optimal
probes.question: What relationship between tokens and trial outcomes is missing from the brief?

probes.trigger: candidate spreads the 15 extra tokens across all three plots
probes.question: How does that choice balance the primary comparison and exploratory work?

probes.trigger: candidate initially totals 95 then corrects the allocation
probes.question: Which priority changes in your revised 90-token plan, and where would you record it?

fair_alternatives: Any complete in-budget allocation within all stated bounds can pass if the trial priorities and missing design information are addressed.
A candidate may recommend seeking more budget; they should still provide a feasible 90-token contingency for the stated task.

Assess the work demonstrated here. Accept relevant examples from education, volunteering, caregiving, placements, or paid work; professional vocabulary and employer pedigree are not evidence of a stronger answer.
reference.assessment_limits: Assess constrained planning, trial priorities, and record integrity using fictional units. Do not offer real irrigation, agronomy, drought response, or environmental compliance advice. Unobserved dimensions are not failures. Credit a reasoned correction and distinguish independently demonstrated reasoning from coached assistance. Do not penalize a candidate for an unrevealed conditional fact; credit appropriate requests and conditional plans, and distinguish candidate assumptions from interviewer-supplied evidence.

interviewer_notes: Assess constrained planning, trial priorities, and record integrity using fictional units. Do not offer real irrigation, agronomy, drought response, or environmental compliance advice. Use only the supplied fictional facts and policies; acknowledge unknowns. Ask one triggered probe at a time after the candidate has finished. Accept plain language and accessible written or spoken explanations. Do not score accent, typing speed, confidence, credentials, or experience with a named employer. Credit revisions and record assistance. All participants are fictional adults; no real patient, client, operational, or confidential data is needed. Allow silence for thinking without treating it as failure. In short sessions prioritize the core decision and one material follow-up, leaving room for a correction and wrap-up.

learning_drills.title: Write a constrained trial plan
learning_drills.prompt: Create a table with requested, minimum, proposed, and actual-to-be-recorded tokens; add a two-sentence approval note. This is self-guided practice; no model assessment is performed.
checklist: Record approved and actual values separately
